note: Window agent corrections, 2 Nov 2026: keyframes whose notes say 'valid for one year' cut back to that span (Swedish 1709, Venetian 1709), Kamchatka kept by Russia, Mughal claim on Kandahar cut, Dzungar occupation of Central Tibet drawn with Tibet as the owner, Chittagong kept by the Mughals and the nawabs. Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: rulings/0 replaced; its 26 cells are the plains round Comilla and Noakhali, Tripura land until 1733 (Tripura page), not the port of Chittagong. Orchestrator 3 Nov 2026: events 0-2 (tibet occupation_end/gain/occupation_start of Dec 1717) dropped: fx-54 E01 made the dossiers record the Dzungar occupation of Tibetan land directly (khoshut loss to tibet, tibet gain, dzungar occupation_start), so the patch would close and reopen the relation.

correction.text: The 1709 shape without the Ukrainian strip and without Tartu; holds 1709 only

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's note says this shape 'holds 1709 only', but the table gives it 1709-1712, so in 1710-1712 it unions the Baltic provinces back into the 1710 and 1712 keyframes and the size rule hands 330 cell-years of Livonia and Estonia from Russia back to Sweden. The page: 'In 1710 the Russian forces captured Riga' and Tallinn, 'the last city, falling in the autumn of 1710'; 'Russia captured Viborg in 1710 and successfully held it against Swedish attempts to retake the town in 1711'.

The dossier's note says the shape holds 1709-1714 ('years only'), but the table gives it 1709-1717, so in 1716-1717 it unions the Morea back into Venice's keyframe (Venice retakes 60 cells from the Ottomans) and the 1718 shape then releases them to nobody. The page: 'Within a hundred days, the entire Peloponnese had been re-taken by the Ottomans' (from 25 June 1715); Passarowitz: 'Morea ceded back to the Ottoman Empire'.

keyframe_overrides.why: Cliopatria's Russian shape omits Kamchatka (1,479 cells), so each keyframe snap releases it to nobody (1,480 cells at 1713) although the ledger gave it to Russia in 1697. The page: '1697-1698: The annexation of Kamchatka by the expedition of Vladimir Atlasov'; the uprising of '1703-1715' was put down ('the Russians crushed the Itelmen uprisings against their rule in 1706'); 'In 1715, the Russians took the largest Koryak settlement, Bolshoy Posad'. It records no loss of Kamchatka. Same repair as p1700-p1709 keyframe_overrides/3 (tsardom-of-russia_1709).
